title: git: Parse delim-pkt and response-end-pkt
description:
Git Protocol version 2[1] defines 0x0001 as a delimiter packet that
separates the sections of a message, as well as 0x0002 as a response_end
packet that indicates the end of a response for stateless connections.

Add parsing and checking of the delim-pkt and response_end-pkt lines,
adding them as items to the tree for ease of reading and filtering while
handling pre-existing "malformed" errors. For additional consistency,
the terminator 0x0000 is now referred to as Flush packet.

[1] https://www.kernel.org/pub/software/scm/git/docs/technical/protocol-v2.html

Part of #17093

Thanks for the quick work. Looks good to go.
Should it be Response end packet rather than this generic Message packet?
In the protocol specification it's presented as "0002 Message Packet (response-end-pkt)" but I don't have any preference, @jrnieder @nasamuffin what do you think?

I had a look at the docs on the Git end (https://git-scm.com/docs/protocol-v2). These refer to 0002 as "Message Packet" like @joeysal indicated - furthermore, they don't refer to it as a "Response End Packet" anywhere, so that string isn't greppable. (although they can grep for "response-end-pkt".)

If *all* the user can see is "Message packet", then I think that's correct, since I'd imagine a user would want to look at Wireshark while cross-referencing with the protocol doc.
Then should the filter be renamed to git.message? I find it quite disturbing to have a filter name that does not match at all the field name.

But it the spec consider that message is a response-end, that's up to you to decide what is acceptable. By the way there is already some inconsistency as packet 0000 is described as flush packet in the spec and is named terminator in the dissector. That's probably something you want to address also.
I agree with Pascal: we can call it something meaningful like "Response end packet" and send a patch to the spec to match.
I agree on the inconsistency with terminator and flush-pkt, should we address that too?
Yes, I think calling git.terminator "Flush packet" in this commit also makes sense. Make sure the commit message says something about it (e.g., "While we're here, <etc>").

changed the description
Should we keep git terminator for backward compatibility or should we rename it to git.flush? As the existing dissector was far from being useful, a rename is probably not an issue.

I think `git.terminator` is a fine name. Working with Git protocol, I'm used to flush-pkt meaning `0000`, but I suspect that if I saw `git.flush` in the wireshark UI I wouldn't immediately make the connection.

What you will see with this change is Flush packet, but the corresponding filter will be git.terminator = 0000. Confusing.
Should not we have a single field Packet type (and a corresponding filter) with value 0000 meaning Flush, 0001 meaning Delimiter and 0002 meaning Response end? A value_string array would be perfect for that. Right now I doubt the filters defined are really useful.

> Should not we have a single field Packet type (and a corresponding filter) with value 0000 meaning Flush, 0001 meaning Delimiter and 0002 meaning Response end? A value_string array would be perfect for that.

+1, that makes a lot of sense to me.

Considering then 
> if I saw `git.flush` in the wireshark UI I wouldn't immediately make the connection

Would this way of renaming them make sense?
- `"git.terminator"` to `"git.flush-pkt"`
- `"git.delimiter"` to `"git.delim-pkt"`
- `"git.response_end"` to `"git.response_end-pkt"`

Then a similar change to the specs document as well

Re:
> have a single field Packet type (and a corresponding filter) with value 0000 meaning Flush, 0001 meaning Delimiter and 0002 meaning Response end? A value_string array would be perfect for that.

I think this means to change the parsing so it'll look for the "Packet type" in a similar way that we look for Git-version/sideband, is that right @pquantin?
